title: Unravel cascading routing fallbacks: postmortem and fixes for misroutes during region drain
creator: Maya Chen
description: Short summary: On 2025-03-06 a routing configuration change combined with a bug in the region drain logic caused large numbers of requests to be misrouted to a single overloaded EU zone, which then triggered cascading fallbacks to cheaper/quantized model variants. This produced increased latencies, elevated error rates (502/504), and several customer-facing timeouts for Dedicated and Hosted API traffic. This ticket documents the postmortem, fixes applied, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-03-06 04:12 UTC - Automated deploy: rollout of routing policy change that sets 'preferred_region' heuristics to prefer cheapest-region when cost-tie
2025-03-06 04:25 UTC - First spike detected: EU region pod group reached 95% GPU utilization; alert routed to oncall (Liam)
2025-03-06 04:27 UTC - 30s window: region drain job triggered to move new sessions away from EU zone; bug in drain algorithm sets region state 'draining' but leaves prefix cache TTL=0
2025-03-06 04:28 UTC - Routing service re-evaluates in-flight batches and misroutes many requests to EU due to race between cache invalidation and policy update (thundering re-eval).

2025-03-06 04:30 UTC - EU overloaded -> fallback policy kicks in: requests are sent to fallback variants (quantized models) but compatibility checks fail for 12% of requests, resulting in 502s and longer P99 latency.
2025-03-06 04:33 UTC - Incident declared (SEV2 -> SEV1), emergency rollback of the routing policy started (Arjun oncall).
2025-03-06 04:40 UTC - Rollback completed; immediate traffic distribution normalizes over 2.5 minutes. Monitoring shows SLO recovery by ~04:45 UTC.
2025-03-06 05:15 UTC - Post-incident emergency fixes deployed: temporary circuit breaker on routing re-eval (30s), and a cooldown window for region drain marking (5m).
2025-03-09 10:00 UTC - Root-cause analysis complete and detailed reproduction added to the repo and chaos tests planned.
root_cause: Multiple interacting issues: 1) The new 'preferred_region' heuristic favored lower-cost regions and was rolled out without a canary to high-traffic tenants; 2) region drain algorithm used a cache invalidation path that set TTL=0 for prefix routing entries, which allowed immediate re-evaluation of routing for many in-flight batches causing a thundering re-evaluation; 3) fallback selection prioritized cost compatibility over model capability, so fallbacks included variants that lacked required tokenizer/config flags leading to compatibility failures. The combination produced a positive feedback loop: misroutes -> overload -> fallbacks -> partial failures -> more retries -> overload.
mitigations_taken: Immediate: rollback of the routing policy change (2025-03-06 04:33 UTC)
Temporary: enabled routing re-eval circuit breaker (30s) and region drain cooldown (5m) to prevent thrash
Hotfix: enforce atomic update of route table to prevent partial writes during drain
Customer comms: notified impacted customers and posted an incident summary in #prod-incidents and sent targeted emails to Dedicated customers
code_fixes: PR #6743 - routing: make cache invalidation atomic and set safe TTLs (merged 2025-03-07) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/6743
PR #6751 - routing: add cooldown window and circuit breaker for region drain (merged 2025-03-07) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/6751
PR #6760 - fallback: change selection priority to capability > latency > cost; add compatibility validation step (merged 2025-03-08) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/6760
monitoring_improvements: New dashboard: Routing Health - key metrics: region_utilization, routing_retries, fallback_rate, fallback_compat_failures (Grafana link added)
Synthetic: add cross-region synthetic traffic that exercises drain and fallback logic every 10 minutes (added to canary)
Tracing: attach route decision reason tag to spans and persist for 72h
postmortem_summary: The outage was caused by a rollout of an insufficiently guarded routing heuristic together with a race in the region drain/caching logic and lax fallback prioritization. The team rolled back the change, deployed targeted fixes that make route updates atomic, added cooldowns/circuit-breakers to prevent re-eval thrash, and reworked fallback selection to ensure capability compatibility before cost. Customer impact was high for a small cohort (high-throughput Dedicated customers and some Hosted API routes); SLOs recovered within ~13 minutes after rollback. Long-term follow-ups include more robust canarying, automated chaos tests for routing state changes, and runbook updates.
action_items: (A1) Add pre-deploy canary gating: route policy changes must pass a 1% traffic canary for 30m before global rollout - owner: Arjun - due: 2025-04-01
(A2) Implement end-to-end chaos tests for region drain and fallback scenarios in CI - owner: Sofia Alvarez - due: 2025-04-15
(A3) Update runbooks: region-drain and routing-thrash runbook with cancellation and rollback steps - owner: Maya Chen - due: 2025-03-20
(A4) Create a dedicated Grafana dashboard and SLO alert for fallback compatibility failures - owner: Platform Observability - due: 2025-03-25
(A5) Post-incident customer outreach for top 5 impacted accounts and offer SLA credit review - owner: Customer Success - due: 2025-03-18
resolution: Root cause fixes merged and deployed in runtime-1.22; monitoring and runbook updates completed. Implemented canary gating and CI chaos tests scheduled. Incident closed after confirmation of SLO stability across 72h monitoring window.
